does: Cuts a small fish open along the belly, takes out the backbone and opens the flesh flat like a book, so that it cooks fast and evenly and takes a marinade, a paste or a stuffing on its whole inner face.

intro.what: A small fish is opened along the belly and its backbone removed while the skin joins the sides.
intro.why: Opening the fish flat creates a broad inner surface for seasoning while teaching careful work around bones and soft flesh.

how: Scale and gut the fish, rinse the belly and pat it dry.
Open the belly from the gut cut to the tail with a small sharp knife and lay the fish open, skin side up, on the board.
Press along the middle of the back with the heel of the hand, so that the backbone loosens and lies flat.
Turn the fish over, lift the backbone from the head end and snip or cut it free at the tail, with the small bones that come with it.
Pull out any bones left in the flesh with the fingertips, and lay the fish flat, skin side down.

cues.text: Both sides lie open in one piece, joined by the skin down the back, with no backbone left.
No bone catches on a fingertip run over the flesh.

mistakes.mistake: Cutting through the skin of the back, so that the halves part.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knife on the belly side and ease the bone out with the fingers.

mistakes.mistake: Pulling the backbone out fast, which tears the soft flesh.
mistakes.fix: Lift it slowly from the head end, and cut it free at the tail.

quiz.question: What shape does butterflying create here?
choices: An opened fish joined along the back.
A whole fish left closed around the backbone.
quiz.because: The fish opens flat while the skin keeps the sides connected.

quiz.question: How should the backbone be freed?
choices: Pull sharply from the tail without supporting the flesh.
Lift slowly from the head end and cut it free at the tail.
Cut through the skin along the back first.
quiz.because: Slow lifting and a controlled final cut limit tearing of the soft flesh.

quiz.question: Which appearance matches the intended preparation?
choices: The sides are separated into loose pieces.
The backbone holds the fish upright.
The sides lie flat together with the backbone removed.
quiz.because: A joined flat shape shows the fish has been opened rather than separated into fillets.

quiz.question: The sides parted because the back skin was cut. What would you change next time?
choices: Work from the belly side and preserve the back skin.
Cut more deeply along the back.
Remove the skin before opening the belly.
quiz.because: The back skin is the connection that keeps the opened fish together.

comes_after.why: The fish is scaled before it is opened, or the scales get everywhere.
The belly is already opened and cleaned when the fish is butterflied.

variant_of.differs: A fillet is cut off the bone as a separate piece, a piece for each side. A butterflied fish stays whole, with both sides joined by the skin along the back, and only the bones are taken out.
